item.title: Kyrgyzstan Leads Region in QR Payments; Irad's Counter Codes Split Two Ways
item.description: Bishkek's fast-growing code payments bring new security worries, while in Irad the choice at the bazaar is a Talasbank card, a Tulpar code or cash.

item.title: US$60 Million Industrial Park Signed for Tash-Kömür; Power Terms to Follow
item.description: The Investment Promotion Office has signed a Dubai-registered developer for a 120-hectare park expected to bring about 900 jobs to Lower Naryn, while Iradenergo says connection terms are still to be set.

item.title: Bishkek Bars Flat Sales Before Walls Stand; Talas Buyers Look at Their Own Sites
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has ended off-plan sales at the foundation stage after more than 40 firms left buyers without flats, and nothing changes in Irad.

item.title: Japan Courts Bishkek for Investment; Irad's Buyers Reach It via Neighbours
item.description: Tokyo wants closer economic ties with Kyrgyzstan, and Irad, where Japan keeps no office, notes the Japanese buyers and scientists it already has.

item.title: Bishkek Links Haulage E-Permits With Six Countries; Irad Trucks Keep Moving
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's electronic permit system will speed customs for six partners, while Irad's hauliers go on working through Kyrgyz-registered firms.

item.title: Bishkek and Tashkent Prosecutors Swap Cyber Expertise; Irad Works Through UNMI
item.description: Irad's own digital services are growing, but its dealings with the neighbours still run through Kara-Oi rather than through ministries.

item.title: Uzbek Inflation Hits 6.5%; Talas Bread and Bus Fares Hold in Som
item.description: A price check at Bazar-i Kalan and the Central Bus Station shows home-made goods and fares steady while dollar-priced imports have moved.

item.title: Bishkek Amends Labour Code on Wage Indexing; Irad Pay Stays Set in Som
item.description: As Kyrgyzstan's president signs the change, the Ministry of Economy restates its line on public pay while the 2027 budget heads to the Mejlis.

item.title: Fog Holds Heating Smoke Over Nurzhan as Air Index Reaches 183
item.description: Irad Gidromet's Sunday readings were the worst of the heating season so far, and residents are advised to keep windows shut in the morning.

item.title: Talas Forum Pitches Rim Orchards and Antimony Processing to Foreign Investors
item.description: Delegates from five neighbouring and partner countries heard the case for turning the ISEZ's farm and ore output into finished goods at home.

item.title: Ankara Party Official Doubts Russia's Observer Case at Turkic States; Irad Watches
item.description: A senior figure in Türkiye's ruling party has questioned whether Russia is eligible for observer status at the Organization of Turkic States, a seat Irad cannot claim for itself.

item.title: Uzbek Cotton Passes 5 Million Tonnes on Half the Land; Irad's Growers Take Note
item.description: A neighbour's first crop of that size in 35 years comes from yield, water and machines, the same three questions facing the Fergana rim.

item.title: Canyon Weekends Bring IS 610,000 to Sary-Bulak District Budget
item.description: Car-park and guide fees at the Kara-Suu Canyon mouth, paid mostly by Talas families and school parties, have funded a gravel car park, bins and a guide.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Banks Drop 284 Firms; Irad Counts Its Payment Routes
item.description: No Iradi company is named in the Bishkek banks' action, and ISEZ lenders say their channels through Almaty and Istanbul are working normally.

item.title: Development Partner Adds US$4.5 Million for Polyclinics and Village Health Posts
item.description: The partner behind the Korgoncho water scheme returns with a second tranche, which the Health Ministry says comes on top of its 2027 budget request.

item.title: Talas Dealer Plans US$3 Million Farm-Machinery Service Centre at Kara-Bulak
item.description: Alatau Agro Machinery, backed by Talasbank and the Rural Development Fund, aims to open repair bays and a parts warehouse before the 2027 spring sowing.

item.title: Kazakh Mining Plans Meet Water Limits; Irad Weighs Sary-Bulak and Chatkal
item.description: A regional opinion piece says the dry south cannot spare the water for new mines, a question Irad's own antimony restart and river schemes share.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Counts 22,000 Legal Workers Abroad; Irad's Migrants Appear in No Count
item.description: A Kyrgyz employment centre says about 22,000 citizens work legally in 26 countries, a figure Irad cannot match because its workers travel on other states' passports.

item.title: Health Ministry Seeks IS 126 Million to Strengthen Clinics and Village Health Posts
item.description: The primary-care line in the draft 2027 budget would pay for equipment, training and a drug reserve, with the aim of easing pressure on the Regional Hospital in Talas.

item.title: Cotton Picking Ends at a Record 41,000 Tonnes on the Fergana Rim
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources says the 2026 raw-cotton crop is the largest in its records since 2007, helped by a summer of steady canal water.

item.title: Moscow Honours Compatriots' Leader in Bishkek; Nurzhan Notes the Neighbour's Council
item.description: The Russian president has decorated the head of Kyrgyzstan's Russian compatriot organisations, a model with no equivalent in Irad.

item.title: Camera Traps Record Two Snow Leopards in Upper Besh-Tash, a First in Decades
item.description: Rangers, TSU scientists and Akjele elders are working out how to keep the cats and the returning flocks apart.

item.title: Uzbek Workers Abroad Halve as Remittances Quadruple; Irad Sees a Familiar Economy
item.description: Tashkent reads the shift as a rise in skilled labour, while Irad's own money from abroad keeps flowing home through Talasbank and Tulpar Pay.

item.title: Migrants' Families Say Cost of Sending Money Home Matters More Than Wages
item.description: With Uzbekistan pressing for bigger remittances, Iradi households that rely on pay from Russia and Kazakhstan are weighing routes, fees and exchange rates.

item.title: Uzbek Grandmaster Beats Three Top Rivals in US Before Title Match; Nurzhan Takes Note
item.description: The neighbouring win lands in Irad's chess city, where players rated under the FIDE flag wonder what an Iradi world-class flag would look like.

item.title: US Transshipment Report Names No Iradi Firm; Talas Watches Origin Rules Abroad
item.description: A White House paper on third-country trade routes touches the paperwork Irad's exports already travel on, and the Ministry of Economy says it is following its neighbours' lead.

item.title: Uzbek Grandmaster Wins US Tournament; Nurzhan's Chess Fans Ask Whose Flag
item.description: A neighbour's last-day victory before the world title match leaves Irad's chess city asking what flag one of its own players would carry.

item.title: After a Comic's Apology to Kazakhstan, Irad Recalls Its Own Screen Portraits
item.description: A British comedian's apology to the Kazakh people has Talas remembering the Swift Hooves cowboys, Homer's kazy and a film it cannot watch at home.

item.title: Kyrgyz Wrestler Wins World Silver in Astana; Irad Again Counts Its Mat Talent Abroad
item.description: A silver for Kyrgyzstan's women's team at the Astana worlds is welcomed in Talas, where Iradi wrestlers compete under neighbours' flags.

item.title: Uzbek Diplomat Named Turkic States Secretary General; Irad Eyes the Rim
item.description: Uzbekistan's deputy foreign minister takes the post for the first time, and Talas weighs what a neighbour's gain means along the 145-km Fergana frontier.
